source_text: In traditional male circumcision rites across sub-Saharan Africa, such as those among the Xhosa in South Africa's Eastern Cape, the procedure is conducted on adolescent boys, typically aged 12-18, as a mandatory initiation into manhood, often bypassing individual informed consent due to overriding cultural and peer pressures that stigmatize uncircumcised males. [122]
